newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate approves Telstra sale.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate approves Telstra sale.

text.p: The Australian Senate approved the A$8 billion (US$6.3 billion) one-third privatisation of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp on Wednesday, opening the way for the biggest share offer in the country's history.

All non-government parties opposed the sale bill, which passed the upper house by a bare margin with the support of two independents, whom the government had wooed with promises of money for their home states.
The sale is the largest in a long line of privatisations that has seen such Australian government assets as Qantas Airways and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia pass into private hands.

Polls showed reform-weary voters were against yet another asset sale but the independent senators said Liberal-National Prime Minister John Howard had gained a mandate in his landslide defeat of the former Labor government in March.
To secure support from voters and the Senate, Howard promised to allocate A$1 billion of the sale proceeds to an environmental repair fund.

When the independents wavered, the government last week boosted that to A$1.1 billion, promising particular attention to the home state of one independent senator, and added a A$250 million fund for rural telecommunications development, answering the concerns of the other independent.
